questions.prompt: After `var x = 10;`, what is true about `x`?
options: Its type is decided at run time from whatever is assigned last
It can later hold a string, because `var` accepts any type
It is inferred as `int` at compile time, and that type is fixed
It is stored as `object` and cast back to `int` when used
questions.explanation: `var` is implicitly typed: the compiler infers the type at compile time from the right-hand expression, and the type can't change afterwards.

questions.prompt: What do you give up by declaring a variable as `dynamic`?
options: The ability to assign a value of a different type later
Compile-time type checking, so mistakes show up as run-time exceptions
The ability to call methods on the variable
Nothing; `dynamic` is just a shorter way to write `var`
questions.explanation: `dynamic` is resolved at run time and the compiler skips type checking, so it is not type safe and risks run-time exceptions. In exchange, its type can change on the fly.

questions.prompt: Which statement about performance and tooling matches the comparison table?
options: `var` is fast with full IntelliSense; `dynamic` is slower because it uses the runtime binder and has limited IntelliSense
`dynamic` is faster because it skips compile-time checks
Both have the same speed and IntelliSense, because both are resolved at compile time
`var` is slower because the compiler must infer the type on every call
questions.explanation: The table marks `var` as fast (no binding needed) with full IntelliSense, and `dynamic` as slower (uses the runtime binder) with limited IntelliSense.

questions.prompt: Which job is the note's example of a good fit for `dynamic` rather than `var`?
options: Holding an anonymous type such as `new { Name = "Aman", Age = 25 }`
Avoiding redundant typing for `new Dictionary<string, List<int>>()`
Storing the result of a LINQ query
COM interop, such as creating `Excel.Application` and setting `excel.Visible = true`
questions.explanation: The usage section lists JSON/`ExpandoObject`, reflection or late-bound APIs and COM interop under `dynamic`; anonymous types, LINQ queries and avoiding redundant typing are listed under `var`.
